name: Golden Path Consumption Practice
description: This practice defines exactly how application developers interact with the IDP to extract value. It covers the creation of opinionated project scaffolding, the abstraction of Dockerfiles via Enterprise Build Strategies (Shipwright/Buildpacks), and the GitOps workflows utilized to deploy microservices rapidly and securely.

narratives.name: The Paved Road Experience
narratives.description: The operational philosophy of how developers consume platform services frictionlessly.

narrativeContexts.context: The primary technological output of the platform engineering organization is the design and implementation of Golden Paths—highly opinionated, fully automated routes for executing common developer tasks.

The underlying philosophy is simple: if application developers choose to stay on the established Golden Path, they are guaranteed a frictionless, highly secure, and fully supported route to production without needing to understand intricate Kubernetes mechanics or complex network routing configurations.

Constructing a robust Golden Path encompasses project templating through intelligent scaffolding engines, automated CI/CD provisioning, inherently baked-in observability, and policy-as-code guardrails.

By deeply focusing on developer psychology and providing a fundamentally safe, zero-configuration method to ship code, the platform team effectively eliminates cognitive load. This confidence directly leads to faster iterations, drastically lower risks of misconfiguration, and a dramatic acceleration in overall organizational delivery velocity as proven by DORA metrics.

patterns.description: The specific scenario demonstrating an application developer onboarding a new microservice rapidly through the IDP Golden Path.

patternViews.name: Developer Cognitive Load Situation
patternViews.description: The developer needs to deploy a complex service but faces massive cognitive load attempting to craft manual Dockerfiles and complex ingress YAML.

narrativeContexts.context: An application developer is tasked with creating a new Java microservice but lacks deep, specialized expertise in writing highly optimized, multi-stage Dockerfiles or managing low-level Kubernetes ingress configurations securely.

Historically, in a non-platformed environment, they would have to file multiple tickets across disconnected infrastructure departments and resort to copying and pasting insecure YAML manifests from legacy repositories, delaying deployment by weeks.

patternViews.name: Self-Service Portal Task
patternViews.description: Utilizing Backstage to trigger the automated creation of the required environment and abstract away the infrastructure details.

narrativeContexts.context: The developer navigates directly to the Internal Developer Portal (Backstage) and selects the standard Java Spring Boot scaffolding template designed by the DevEx team.
By simply providing the target Git repository URL, the developer initiates the Golden Path, offloading the heavy configuration burden entirely to the platform's automated logic.

patternViews.name: Automated Scaffolding Action
patternViews.description: The platform engine leverages Shipwright, Cloud Native Buildpacks, and GitOps to autonomously deploy the asset.

narrativeContexts.context: The portal automatically generates the repository, linking it to a robust CI pipeline that compiles the code and builds a secure OCI image via Cloud Native Buildpacks (Shipwright).
Crucially, comprehensive observability endpoints and declarative HTTPRoute definitions are dynamically injected into the deployment manifests, baking in best practices without manual intervention.

patternViews.name: Velocity Increase Result
patternViews.description: The service is live, strictly secure-by-default, and organizational DORA metrics improve exponentially.

narrativeContexts.context: An intelligent GitOps controller residing securely inside the cluster detects the new manifests and autonomously synchronizes the live cluster state with the Git repository.

As a direct result, the developer’s "Time to First Service" drops precipitously from weeks to minutes. Cognitive load is effectively eliminated, and organizational DORA metrics—specifically Deployment Frequency and Lead Time—increase dramatically.
